sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Tricep Banded Kickback is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps, with particular emphasis on the lateral head, by extending the arm back against band tension.

Performed in a hinged position with the upper arm pinned to the torso, it produces peak contraction at lockout and a strong pump.

It is a joint-friendly accessory movement for adding arm size, elbow extension strength, and upper-body detail.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Targets the triceps with peak contraction at lockout
- Accommodating band tension through the range of motion
- Low-impact and joint-friendly
- Portable and equipment-efficient
- Trains scapular stability through the hinge position
- Easily scaled by changing band thickness or stance
- Great finisher for upper-body training

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Triceps Brachii (all three heads, emphasis on Lateral Head)

Secondary: Rear Deltoids, Core, Forearms

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Step on the band with one or both feet to anchor it.
2. Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, chest up.
3. Grasp the handle(s) with a neutral grip.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Pin the upper arm tight to the side of the torso.
2. Bend the elbow to about 90 degrees.
3. Brace the core and pack the shoulder.

sections.heading: Kickback
sections.content:
1. Exhale and extend the arm straight back until the elbow locks out.
2. Keep the upper arm still; only the forearm moves.
3. Squeeze the triceps hard at full extension.

sections.heading: Return and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Inhale and bend the elbow back to 90 degrees under control.
2. Maintain tension on the band throughout.
3. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Allowing the upper arm to drop or swing
- Rounding the lower back in the hinge
- Using momentum instead of controlled triceps extension
- Shrugging the shoulder during the rep
- Using a band that is too heavy and breaking form
- Incomplete lockout at the top
- Losing core bracing during the set

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Resistance Band with Handles (or loop band)
- Athletic shoes for secure footing
- Optional: Lighter and heavier bands for progression
- Optional: Mirror to monitor form

sections.heading: Band Adjustments
sections.content:
1. Step on the band with a comfortable stance width.
2. Wider stance creates more tension; narrower stance reduces it.
3. Choose a band thickness appropriate for your strength level.
4. Confirm grip on the handle(s) is secure before starting.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Staggered or parallel, depending on preference.
2. Torso: Hinged forward, flat back, chest up.
3. Upper Arm: Pinned tight to the torso, parallel to the floor.
4. Shoulders: Packed and down, not shrugged.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes slightly ahead of the hands.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Dumbbell Tricep Kickback: Free-weight variation
- Cable Tricep Kickback: Cable variation with constant tension
- Tricep Pushdown: Standing cable triceps isolation
- Overhead Tricep Extension: Long-head focused variation
- Bench Dips: Bodyweight triceps movement
- Close-Grip Bench Press: Compound triceps movement

sections.content:
Two-Arm Band Kickback: Described here
Single-Arm Band Kickback: Unilateral variation
Bench-Supported Band Kickback: Chest supported on a bench
Tempo Band Kickback: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy
Pause Band Kickback: Pause at peak contraction
Kneeling Band Kickback: Kneeling variation for stability

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Elbow Pain: Lighten the band and keep the upper arm still
Lower Back Issues: Shorten the hinge or use a bench-supported variation
Shoulder Issues: Keep the shoulder packed and reduce range
Band Too Light: Step wider or use a heavier band
Band Too Heavy: Use a lighter band or narrower stance
Beginners: Start with a light band to learn the pattern
